name: Five-link coilover (Grzyb & Kowalski 2001 rear geometry; aftermarket coilover and rear bar)
source: A. Grzyb, M. Kowalski, 'Optimisation of five-link suspension mechanism of a vehicle solid tyres', Engineering Transactions 49(1), 47-63, 2001 (IPPT PAN). doi:10.24423/engtrans.573.2001 https://et.ippt.pan.pl/index.php/et/article/view/573. Optimized link points (p.57-58); the wheel center is the axis point B7 (the travel point of the paper), the spin axis B6 to B7. Axes: x forward (assumed; the paper does not state the sense), y toward the wheel, z up. The radius 302 mm puts the ground at z = 0 (assumed; the paper gives no radius). Masses, spring points, and rates are assumed. Library model: the geometry is the validation model in tests/data/multibody/grzyb_five_link; masses, spring and damper rates, and stops are assumed for the dynamics. Coilover library model: the validated five-link geometry with a direct-acting coilover on the knuckle (spring 50 N/mm, 32-click damper adjustable in bump and rebound) and a rear anti-roll bar with drop links to the knuckles. The rates, the damper curves, and the bar geometry are assumed values, not measured parts.

spring.note: spring points assumed (not in the source)

damper.note: damper force (N) against shaft speed (mm/s, + rebound); a digressive street/track coilover curve of 1.94 / 5 N.s/mm (bump / rebound) below the 100 mm/s knee and 0.7 / 1.65 N.s/mm above it (assumed curve, no dyno data)

stops.note: coilover bump stop 50 mm from static: a progressive polyurethane stop (150 N/mm and 2000 N/mm^2, assumed)

camber_shim.note: eccentric on the upper link 5 (assumed adjuster)

arb.note: bar torsion rate N.m/rad (a 16 mm bar); the 200 mm arms and the 1.41 m track give about 520 N.m/deg of axle roll stiffness; drop link from the bar arm to the knuckle (assumed geometry)
